title: GitHub is switching its leaked-password checks to a new AI model that can spot passwords with no standard format.
key_facts: GitHub's fine-tuned model reads surrounding code to identify likely credentials.
It finds passwords that have no recognisable token format.
Existing AI-detected secret alert scans switch to the new model at no additional charge for GHSP and GHAS customers.
New AI push protection and the security review checks consume AI Credits and are opt-in.
Administrators can disable the new capabilities by policy and set budgets.
The model also brings AI-detected alerts to GHES 3.23 in public preview.
quote_evidence: It reads surrounding code to identify likely credentials, including passwords without a recognizable token format, without generating code or prose.
The new opt-in checks for push protection and the security review command will consume GitHub AI Credits.
why_it_matters_hint: Leaked passwords are a common route into company systems, so earlier detection matters to any team that stores code on GitHub.
